Photon: global illumination in Doppio

Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21

Indirect light, colour bleeding and sky occlusion without ray-tracing hardware, and the Photon tab that manages it.

Photon is the engine's global illumination (GI). Doppio edits it from the Photon tab (View menu, next to the generators) and from the Photon GI component in the Inspector: both write the same fields, so they never disagree.

1. How Photon works#

Part What it does
Near field Screen-anchored radiance cascades (K to 0) traced against the depth buffer, merged front to back and resolved to SH-L1 probes (photon_cascade.comp, photon_c0.comp)
Far field Four clipmap levels of voxels (cells of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 m, 64 cubed each) with a lattice of probes per level; rays that leave the screen query it
Material volume The albedo and coverage of the scene's surfaces, written by the triangle voxeliser (photon_voxelize_tri.comp) and by the screened fill
Injection The sun, point and spot lights, and the sky, are injected into the voxel faces with a shadow marched through the material volume (photon_inject.comp)
Feedback The previous frame's irradiance is fed back with a cap and a reprojected history, which is the multi-bounce
Temporal average Every probe offsets its traced directions by its own fixed amount, so the noise is not coherent; the resolve averages the reprojected irradiance of the previous frame into this one (weight 0.4 while the scene changes, 0.07 when still, quicker for large differences), and the far probes follow the same weight

The screen cascades dominate what the camera sees. The far field is what lights a surface from things the camera does not see: the wall behind it, the underside of a ceiling, the sun's bounce through a slit.

2. The Photon tab#

The tab edits the first Photon GI component of the scene (the renderer reads the last enabled one, so keep one). Add Photon GI creates it on a new entity (on, compute path, High quality) when the scene has none. Every edit goes through the engine's component API and records one undo step (a slider is one step per field, not per value).

Control Field What it does
Enabled Enabled Photon on or off
Path Path The screen fallback gather, or the compute cascades with the voxel far field
Quality Quality Off, Low, Balanced, High or Eco: probe spacing and cascade count
Intensity Intensity Multiplier of the indirect light, near field and far field alike
Bounce gain Bounce gain Scales the light the voxels hold (see section 4)
Sky Sky intensity The sky light a ray finds when it leaves the screen and the voxels
Ambient Ambient An extra ambient bounce added to the fallback
Radius Radius Reach of the screen cascades, in world units
Skinned meshes Voxel skinned meshes Skinned meshes in the volume, in their current pose
Cut-out meshes as solid Voxel cut-out meshes Foliage cards count as solid blocks (off by default)
Terrain Voxel terrain Terrain meshes in the volume
Full rebuilds Full rebuilds Diagnostic: rebuild every level on every change
Rebuild voxels Throw the volume away; the next frame voxelises the scene again
View Debug view Lit scene, GI only, or the sky fallback only

3. What is in the voxel volume#

The triangle voxeliser writes the scene's geometry into the volume, including what the camera never sees:

  • Opaque meshes always, with the colour of their material times the mean colour of its picture (mid grey when the picture cannot be read), per material slot. Blended surfaces are not solid and stay out.
  • Terrain from its mesh, with an earth colour taken from its tint (its splat layers are not one picture).
  • Skinned meshes in the pose of the frame; they are revoxelised where they move.
  • Cut-out meshes only when the switch is on: foliage cards then shade like solid blocks.
  • Water and volumetric lights never.

Dirty regions#

Each object has a hash of its mesh, transform, pose and colour. A frame where nothing changed costs one hash per object. When an object moves, the voxeliser clears and revoxelises only the boxes where it was and where it is, in all four levels (each box padded by one cell of the level); at most eight boxes, beyond that the levels rebuild whole. A level also rebuilds whole when its clipmap origin moves. The panel shows both counts.

The 1 million triangle cap#

Above 1 million triangles the voxeliser does not run and only the screened fill remains (it covers what the camera sees). The panel shows Over 1M triangles: screen fill only and the engine reports over_budget. Nothing is dropped silently.

What it costs: probes outside the view and coarse levels#

The far field traces 16,384 probes (4 levels of 16 cubed), about 100 rays each, so it was the biggest cost of Photon (25 ms at 720p on the benchmark scene). A surface the camera sees reads the probes within about one spacing of it, so:

  • A probe more than 1.8 spacings outside the camera's frustum is not traced: its tile is carried over from the previous frame and its SH is left as it was. A probe that was out of view for more than 120 frames starts from a fresh trace when it comes back.

  • While the scene is calm (the temporal weight below 0.2) level 1 and level 2 are traced every second frame and level 3 every fourth, with the previous frame's weight raised to the period so they converge as fast per second. While anything changes every level follows every frame.

  • The border texels of a probe's tile repeat the nearest of the 8 by 8 interior directions, so they copy what the interior traced instead of tracing 36 more rays.

  • While the camera is still and the scene calm, the screen cascades 2 and up are also traced on alternate frames (they keep their atlas in between); a moving camera rebuilds them every frame.

The probe pass fell from 25 to about 7 ms, the near field from 12.7 to about 7 ms, and the regression scenes of section 8 still pass. The Profiler lists each pass (Photon::probes, Photon::inject, one scope per cascade); with GPU timing on they are real GPU times.

4. Bounce gain#

Bounce gain multiplies the light injected into the voxels (the sun, the lights and the sky ambient), so the bounce between surfaces grows without touching the direct light. It does not scale the screen cascades, which follow Intensity. Measured on the far floor of a closed room with a slit in the ceiling, GI only, out of 255:

Bounce gain 0 1 4
Far floor 13 18 24

With gain 0 what remains is the screen cascades and the sky fallback; the gain moves the far field's share (the part above the gain-0 level).

The weather and the bounce#

The Environment tab's weather reaches Photon through the light it already reads, so nothing is baked:

  • Moving cloud shadows. With the clouds' ground shadows on, the injection pass multiplies the sun by the cloud shadow at each voxel (the same function the forward shaders use), so the bounce off the ground follows the cloud's shadow as it drifts. The near field reads the forward pass's direct light and follows it already.
  • Lightning. A flash adds a cold directional light for its length, which Photon injects like the sun, and multiplies its sky radiance (the sky flashes too), so the bounce flashes with the strike and falls back with it.
  • Overcast and fog grey and tint Photon's sky light (see the Environment guide).

The drift of the cloud shadows is deliberately not part of the light hash (it would hold the temporal average in its fast mode all the time): the resolve follows a large difference between history and present on its own, so a slow drift stays smooth, while a flash adds a light, changes the hash and is followed at once.

5. Presets#

Every preset switches Photon on, on the compute path.

Preset Quality Radius Sky Ambient Bounce gain Notes
Balanced Balanced 14 0.65 0.2 1 The default look
Interior (strong bounce) High 10 0.35 0.1 2 Rooms lit through openings
Outdoor High 40 0.8 0.25 1 Long reach, strong sky
Fast (Eco) Eco 14 0.65 0.2 1 Skinned meshes and terrain left out of the volume
Diagnostic (GI only) High 14 0.65 0.2 1 GI only view and full rebuilds

6. Voxel statistics#

The Voxel volume card reads the engine's counters every frame (no GPU read-back):

Line Meaning
Objects, Triangles What the volume was built from (triangles are 0 while over budget)
Levels rebuilt (last) One bit per level rebuilt whole in the latest update
Regions (last / total) Boxes revoxelised in the latest update, and since the session began
Whole levels (total) Level rebuilds since the session began
Update time CPU time to encode the latest update
Far field running The far field ran in the latest frame

What it costs, and what it does not: each view that uses Photon (the editor Viewport, the Gameplay tab, the Camera tab) has its own instance, because the targets are sized to the view and the far field is centred on its camera; one shared instance made two views of different sizes or places rebuild each other's targets and voxels every frame. In a still scene with a still camera the far field is left as it is once it has converged (48 frames, with a real trace every 240), and while the camera only turns, in a calm scene, it is traced every other frame. The engine counts both (far_skipped, far_half_rate, target_rebuilds in the C ABI's Photon stats). On a sun, a camera and a cube at 1158 x 536 the editor frame went from 14.4 ms to 4.1 ms still and to 10.0 ms turning, and three views from 43.5 ms to 9.2 ms still; cargo test -p doppio-ui --lib -- --ignored --nocapture frame_budget:: prints these with the engine's profiler.

7. For agents and tests#

The same commands are agent actions (--features agent), each returning a Message:

Action or query Args
show_photon, photon_add, photon_rebuild none
photon_set { "field": "Bounce gain", "value": 2.5 } (a bool, a number, or an option name or index)
photon_preset { "name": "Interior (strong bounce)" }
query photon The settings and statistics, or { "present": false }

The headless flows are doppio/tests/ui-flows/photon-panel.json and photon-scene.json; the images of this page come from caffeine-website/captures/flows/capture-photon-docs.json (./scripts/capture-photon-docs.sh).

C ABI v17#

c
CaffeineResult caffeine_session_photon_stats(const CaffeineSession*, CaffeinePhotonStats* out);
CaffeineResult caffeine_session_photon_rebuild(CaffeineSession*);

CaffeinePhotonStats holds objects, triangles, over_budget, far_enabled, full_rebuilds, region_rebuilds, last_level_mask, last_regions and last_update_ms. Rust reads it as Engine::photon_stats().

8. Tests and limits#

  • GPU tests (tests/test_photon_voxelizer.cpp): voxels of a triangle, a wall behind the camera, clipmap moves, the sun's injection, probes in front of a red wall, a closed room, the mean colour of a picture, a moving object revoxelising only its box (identical, voxel for voxel, to a rebuild from scratch) and the cap.
  • Regression scenes (photon_gi in windows/main/tests.rs): colour bleed, an off-screen sunlit wall, a sealed room, a thin wall, the debug views and the bounce gain; and photon_panel: add, edit, undo, rebuild and a moving object.
  • Limits: no motion vectors yet (the history reprojects with the previous matrix), the terrain has one colour, a cut-out mesh is a solid block, and a change (a light that moved) takes about twenty frames to settle in, because the resolve averages frames.

See also the graphics roadmap and the editor page for Photon.
